key_insight: Annotators produce free-text explanations that reveal individual reasoning preferences, and this paper investigates whether LLMs can learn annotator-specific label+explanation behavior. The authors analyze per-annotator stability and propose a cross-annotator preference optimization approach to model those differences.
problem_solved: Addresses the challenge of modeling and reproducing annotator-specific reasoning (free-text explanations) beyond simple label disagreement, enabling systems to capture human label variation at the explanation level.
method: Collect sentence-pair data for two tasks (natural language inference and paraphrase judgment) with four annotators each, including labels and free-text explanations.
Analyze annotator-level stability to assess whether individual explanation patterns exist and can be learned.
Train LLMs with a Cross-Annotator Preference Optimization objective to encourage the model to reproduce annotator-specific label+explanation behavior.
impact: Provides a path toward personalized and more faithful explanation generation that respects individual annotator preferences, improving dataset understanding, model auditing, and human–AI alignment. Useful for practitioners building explainable models or aggregating multi-annotator data.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: data (pairs + annotator explanations) → stability analysis → cross-annotator preference optimization → annotator-specific outputs
Bar/heatmap comparing per-annotator pattern stability and inter-annotator disagreement
Before/after examples: identical input with different annotator explanations and the model’s corresponding personalized outputs
Icon set: annotator avatars, explanation bubbles, optimization/learning icon, evaluation/checkmark
paper_title: Human Label Variation as Stable Signal: Learning Annotator-Specific Explanation Behavior via Cross-Annotator Preference Optimization
paper_authors: Beiduo Chen, Pingjun Hong, Ziyun Zhang, Benjamin Roth, Anna Korhonen
